expr: (list (progn (string-match "\\(a\\)\\(b\\)" "ab") (replace-match "\\2\\1" t nil "ab")) (progn (string-match "b+" "abbbc") (replace-match "[\\&]" t nil "abbbc")) (progn (string-match "b" "ab") (replace-match "\\\\" t nil "ab")))
note: LITERAL nil's THREE ESCAPES. Emacs answers ("ba" "a[bbb]c" "a\\"): `\\N' is the Nth group's text, `\\&' is the whole match, and `\\\\' is one backslash. The same three `replace-regexp-in-string' already implements in kg (phase15-replace-regexp-in-string, an agreement), which is where 26.2 should take the expansion from rather than writing a second one. kg answered `void-function' before 26.2 and answers ("ba" "a[bbb]c" "a\\\\") now, taking the expansion from `internal--replace-expand' exactly as this note said it should. The third element also brushes fe's writer divergence -- a printed kg string does not re-escape its backslashes -- and it did NOT bite: both sides print the same thing.
